summary.headline: Viyash Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.2% YoY to INR 988 crores, with pre-ESOP EBITDA of INR 208 crores and net debt cut to INR 26 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 988 crores (up 16.2% YoY, up 4.4% QoQ) and PAT was INR 85 crores (up 16.1%). Gross margin eased to 53.7% from 55.5% a year ago, which management attributed to a one-off US exclusivity launch in Q2 FY26 and to solvent and raw-material cost inflation. BioForLife Italia was acquired at 100% effective 1 October 2026 and will be consolidated from Q3 FY27. Net debt fell to INR 26 crores from INR 166 crores at March 2026. Management guided to 20%+ revenue growth for FY27 and an API H2 pickup, while the US business is guided to about 10% growth.

segments.name: US formulation (human health)
segments.commentary: Revenue was about INR 110-115 crores run rate per quarter after a one-off exclusivity product in Q2 FY26 (about USD 5 million at 90%+ gross margin) normalised. FY26 US revenue was about INR 426 crores; management guides to about 10% growth, which the analyst's calculation put at about 15%.

segments.name: Animal health / companion animal
segments.commentary: Companion animal H1 FY27 sales were about USD 20 million, with FY27 guided to about USD 30 million including BioForLife (about 60% growth). Animal health API is guided to grow 20%+.

segments.name: API and CDMO
segments.commentary: Management says FY27 API revenue is tracking 12-13% growth, with H2 stronger than H1; Q2 grew about 10-12% and Q1 was weak due to geopolitical disruption and customer destocking. Combined human and animal API was about INR 1,500 crores in FY26; the split is about 55% formulation and 43-45% API.

segments.name: Europe and emerging markets formulation
segments.commentary: Emerging markets grew about 39-40% YoY in H1, led by Brazil volumes and Turkey new products. Europe growth is guided to double digits even in constant currency, with management no longer sure of an earlier 18-20% guidance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ expected, per management's answer to a question on top-line growth.
FY27 PAT expected to grow more than 50%, with H2 expected to be strong.
US business expected to grow about 10% in FY27 (about INR 480-490 crores implied) and about 10% growth in the US business overall, with no major US launch in FY27.
API expected to grow 12-13% in FY27 with H2 stronger than H1; animal health API guided to 20%+ growth.
Gross margin expected to stay around 54-55% in FY27 and FY28, with exclusive launches as the main upside.
Companion animal capex of about INR 140-150 crores in FY27, and about INR 150 crores over the next two years; growth capex to be partly offset by the Ambernath repurposing.
Goodwill amortisation of about INR 8.9 crores in Q2 and about INR 4 crores in Q3 FY27, after which it ends.
Normalised ESOP cost of about INR 148-149 crores in FY27 and about INR 32 crores in FY28, settling at about INR 25 crores steady state.
Vietnam commercial sales expected from early next year; Europe launch of a big API product expected next year.
Oncology finished dose pipeline and companion animal blockbuster launches expected to contribute materially from 2029-2030 (FY30).
Aspiration of USD 1 billion revenue by 2032, implying about 17-18% CAGR.
capex_capacity: Companion animal dedicated manufacturing facility at Ambernath being built; commissioning expected by Q1 FY28, ahead of 2029 launches; a Turkey partner facility is the backup route.
Animal health R&D spend is running at about INR 10 crores per quarter, at least INR 40 crores annualised, up from INR 3-4 crores per quarter before the merger; the animal health R&D team has doubled.

One new manufacturing line for animal health (2029-30 launches) to start in FY28 and finish in FY28; animal health capacity expanded 20-25% for the next 1-2 years; Albendazole capacity more than doubled.
New oncology finished dose R&D centre in Hyderabad, handling high-potent products up to OEB 5 for pilot-scale batches.
Solar capacity: 2.3-2.5 MW to be commissioned this month, with another 4-5 MW targeted by year-end.
demand_pricing: Raw-material and solvent prices rose due to the war, costing about 0.3-0.4% of gross margin in Q2; some increases were passed on to customers but not all.
API customers with mature products cut inventory in H1, which weighed on Q1 volumes; Q2 improved but was not fully recovered.
Human health: a delayed iron complex product, expected to contribute in H2 FY27 rather than H1.
US generic penetration is about 15-20%; Europe generic volume share is about 50-60%, with management expecting 70-80% after the 2029-30 launches.
Companion animal: about USD 3 billion brand value for three to four targeted molecules; targeted market about USD 1.5 billion ex-US, with about 40% expected price erosion at generics.
Companion animal API: management says one or two products are supplying qualification quantities; blockbusters such as Laners and oclacitinib are not yet supplied.

qa_highlights.question: Why did US business decline YoY and QoQ, and what growth is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 FY26 included a one-off exclusive launch (about USD 5 million at 90%+ gross margin) that has since normalised; current run rate is about INR 100-115 crores per quarter and FY27 US growth is guided at about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex guidance for the next three years, and what is left of goodwill amortisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Companion animal and related capex is about INR 140-150 crores in FY27 and about INR 150 crores over two years (may be lower). Goodwill amortisation was INR 8.9 crores in Q2, and INR 4 crores is expected in Q3, after which it ends.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company protect CDMO and API relationships as companion animal molecules go off-patent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most CDMO revenue is from mature farm-animal products; companion animal API is at an early stage, with one or two products in qualification quantities, and qualification typically takes about five years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the API business and the segment split?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 is expected to be much better than H1, with API growth of 12-13% guided. The formulation-to-API split is about 55:43 now and is expected to stay similar near term, with formulation growing faster after 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin dip, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the 53.7% margin to the base effect of last year's one-off US launch, raw material and solvent inflation (0.3-0.4%), and minor product mix. It guided to 54-55% for the next two years, with exclusive launches as upside.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18-20% Europe growth guidance still valid, and when will oncology contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe is expected to grow double digits even in constant currency, and oncology is expected to contribute materially from 2029-2030 (FY30).

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more acquisitions, and what is the priority?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acquisitions are being explored, with market access the first priority and product gap-filling second; a sizable deal is expected next year. Mr. Haribabu also said next year may be the peak for acquisitions, with debt repayment (about INR 120 crore India loan) considered in later years.

risks_watch: Gross margin: Q2 was 53.7% and sits below the 55% level; watch raw material and solvent inflation and the mix shift.
API H2 ramp: H1 API growth was about 8%, and FY27 guidance depends on a heavier H2 with customer procurement recovering.
US business: revenue is down YoY because of the Q2 FY26 exclusivity base; guidance is about 10% growth with no big FY27 launch.
Human health iron complex launch has slipped from H1 to H2 FY27.
Execution risk on the Ambernath companion animal facility (commissioning Q1 FY28) and the Turkey partner backup site.
Acquisition-led growth and the 20%+ growth target depend on deals that may be sizable next year; funding and integration of BioForLife need watching.
Shareholding: Carlyle is an investor since 2021; management said no exit expected in the next 12 months, but the company is open to discussion on block sales.
key_quotes: We believe H2 will also show strong performance, and overall year PAT actually is going to grow more than 50%.
API, first question to answer, second half is going to be much better than first half, that I can tell you.
Still we are in a strong position on that product.
Straight answer is yes. We are exploring continuously on that.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth, H2 API recovery and the companion animal launch pipeline, backed by specific timelines and capex figures. Cautious and evasive on the US Q2-on-Q2 decline, the Europe 18-20% guidance (management did not recall it), and the Carlyle stake exit, where it said only that nothing was expected in the next 12 months.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ (raised), backed partly by H1 growth of 17.8%, companion animal API tracking 20%+, and Europe/emerging markets growth; API guide is mid-teens/12-13% and US ~10%, so the 20%+ group guide relies on animal health and BioForLife consolidation from Q3, with specifics on Ambernath capacity only from FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell to 53.7% from 55.5% YoY and management guides 54-55% for FY27-FY28, with EBITDA margin 21.1% vs 22.1%; solvent/raw-material inflation cost 0.3-0.4% of gross margin in Q2, and only exclusive launches are upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ambernath companion animal facility (about INR 140-150 crores capex in FY27) is under construction with commissioning guided by Q1 FY28; one animal health line starts and finishes in FY28 and animal health capacity is expanded 20-25%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ with H1 at 17.8%, API growth of 12-13% with H2 stronger than H1 (Q2 grew about 10-12%), and emerging markets up about 39-40% in H1; BioForLife consolidated from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at about INR 150 crores over two years and the Ambernath build is already under way, so a new major capex is not guided; a peak acquisition year is flagged for next year, which may bring deal capex rather than plant capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guide was raised to 20%+ and H1 was 17.8%, but US is guided only ~10%, API mid-teens to 12-13%, and the 20%+ depends on animal health and BioForLife consolidation from Q3.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: API H1 growth was only about 8%, the iron complex launch slipped to H2 FY27, the Q2 US run rate is INR 100-115 crores per quarter, and Europe 18-20% guidance was not recalled by management.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Iron complex human health product slipped into H2 FY27, Vietnam commercial sales from early next year, and a big Europe API product launch next year; no major US launch in FY27.

rows.label: Vietnam commercial sales and Europe API launch
rows.why: Management expects Vietnam commercial sales from early next year and a big Europe API product launch next year, adding to the growth pipeline.

rows.label: Acquisition-led growth; peak deal year FY28
rows.why: Management said next year may be the peak year for acquisitions, with a sizable deal expected; BioForLife Italia (100%) consolidated from Q3 FY27, and the INR 120 crore India loan repayment is deferred to later years.

rows.label: Net debt cut to INR 26 crores
rows.why: Net debt fell from INR 166 crores at March 2026 to INR 26 crores at 30 Sep 2026, about 0x LTM EBITDA, leaving room for acquisitions.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20%+ FY27 growth, H2 API recovery, and the companion animal pipeline with specific timelines and capex; it was cautious on the US Q2 decline, evasive on the Europe 18-20% guidance and the Carlyle stake exit, while analysts pressed on gross margin, US growth and API H2 ram
